question: A 66-year-old man presents to his family physician complaining of a sandpaper-like sensation when he touches the lesion on his forehead. His medical history is relevant for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, for which he is taking losartan and atorvastatin. He used to work as a gardener, but he retired 3 years ago. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination of his forehead reveals male-pattern baldness and thin, adherent, yellow-colored skin lesions that feel rough to the touch (see image). His family physician refers to him to a dermatologist for further management and treatment. Which of the following conditions would the patient most likely develop if this skin condition is left untreated?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Chronic sun exposure -> Actinic keratosis -> Squamous cell carcinoma -> 80% CHAIN: Seborrheic keratosis -> Lesions can mimic other skin conditions -> Delayed diagnosis of skin cancer -> 70% CHAIN: Hypercholesterolemia -> Xanthelasma formation -> Increased risk of atherosclerosis -> 80%
enhanced_information: The patient is most likely to develop squamous cell carcinoma if the skin condition is left untreated. Chronic sun exposure can lead to actinic keratosis, which is a precursor to squamous cell carcinoma. The presence of seborrheic keratosis can mimic other skin conditions, potentially delaying the diagnosis of skin cancer. Xanthelasma formation in hypercholesterolemia increases the risk of atherosclerosis but is not directly related to the development of skin cancer in this case.
analysis: The patient's presentation of thin, adherent, yellow-colored skin lesions on the forehead, along with a sandpaper-like sensation, is consistent with seborrheic keratosis. Although seborrheic keratosis itself is benign and does not progress to skin cancer, it can mimic other skin conditions, potentially delaying the diagnosis of skin cancer. In this case, chronic sun exposure could lead to actinic keratosis, a precursor to squamous cell carcinoma. Therefore, if left untreated, the patient is most likely to develop squamous cell carcinoma.
